docs.title: FontLab App
docs.text:
fontlab-fontlabapp provides the fontlabapp package: shared FontLab application, UI, drawing, reporting and guarded editing helpers. It supplies reusable mechanics for Fly, Fontport, Glyport and FontLab scripts. Python 3.11 arm64 is the host target. The package declares Python >=3.11 and requires fontlab-python-pens>=1.0.0. Fontport remains optional through the fontport extra.

The host-free smallcap_consistency engine reports exporting case counts, missing and orphan smallcaps, legacy capital/lowercase coverage and two-sided kerning-group differences. The legacy_lowercase_without_smallcaps section independently requires an exporting .sc glyph even when modern .smcp coverage passes. smallcap_capture.current_report() lazily captures the current font and master within a shared three-second budget. Export scope is explicitly the public.skipExportGlyphs compatibility policy; unknown mappings and ambiguous groups are disclosed. Native qualification remains pending.

Pure utility modules load outside FontLab. Native operations require FontLab's fontlab, FL, fontgate, fontpr and PythonQt APIs as used by each operation. Native modules and panels load on demand. General UI belongs here; FontParts/UFO adapters belong in Fontport; Glyphs.app compatibility belongs in Glyport. App never imports Glyport. Optional Fontport imports are confined to fontui; base App still installs without Fontport. Scriptmix scripts and App's own Scripts/ access App through fly.ap.

docs.title: Find the right surface
docs.text:
• Install and use App with the host interpreter and lazy imports.
  • Domains and shared UI separates App, Fontport and Glyport responsibilities.
  • Plugmix retains all 39 reporter descriptions and four other plugin kinds.
  • Complete API map lists all 1025 modules and their public names.
  • Complete runtime reference retains every usage, migration and writer qualification from the maintained README.
  • Background tools retain their explicit N86 HOLD and N92 source-review blocker.

Source and ordinary Qt checks do not establish native FontLab behavior. Private Pages configuration and publication remain owner-held.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Run from this repository. Set FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH to an existing writable directory on your external scratch volume. Use a fresh writable cache and an existing writable TMPDIR there. uv needs network access for packages not cached. Build from reviewed Git history so hatch-vcs supplies the genuine version required by the local Fontport/Glyport dependency floor. Do not reuse a cache containing App metadata from another build.

: "${FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH:?Set FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH to your external scratch directory}"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH/app-doc-check-cache"
export TMPDIR="$FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$UV_CACHE_DIR" "$TMPDIR"
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1
uv venv --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none "$TMPDIR/app-venv"
uv pip install --python "$TMPDIR/app-venv/bin/python" -e '.[test]'
uv pip install --python "$TMPDIR/app-venv/bin/python" -e ../fontlab-fontport -e ../fontlab-glyport
uv pip install --python "$TMPDIR/app-venv/bin/python" --no-deps -e ../fontlab-fly
"$TMPDIR/app-venv/bin/python" -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider

Install Fontport and Glyport with their dependencies (defcon, fissix, fontpens, glyphsLib); without them two tests fail. The tests of the FontParts editors (tests/test_ui_*.py, tests/test_cov_ui_*.py) call pytest.importorskip("fontlab_fontport"): they skip, not fail, when Fontport is absent, so a plain ./test.sh run does not exercise them. ./test.sh installs the sibling Fontport and Glyport checkouts editable and puts the sibling Fly source on PYTHONPATH when they exist, so it runs the whole suite; the test extra itself does not list Fontport.

The plain test-extra environment previously gave 6240 passes and three failures because Fly was missing. ./test.sh uses uv run --extra test with editable sibling Fontport/Glyport when available and sibling Fly on PYTHONPATH; the explicit environment above also verifies an installed Fly. Use the explicit command for the full suite. pytest reads tests/ and adds src to its import path.

There is a separate tests_docs/ suite for the documentation site. With the same exports, run the README migration contract and public-surface/dependency checks:

uv run --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none --no-project --with-editable '.[test]' python -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_public_surface.py tests/test_package_boundaries.py tests/test_tombstones.py
uv run --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none --no-project --with-editable '.[test]' python -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_public_surface.py::test_readme_when_read_then_moved_table_names_every_tombstone
uv run --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none --no-project --with ruff==0.14.10 ruff check --no-cache --select F821 src tests Scripts

The lint command checks undefined names; there is no configured full lint gate. Offline tests cover Python logic and doubles. Standalone Qt uses a different binding. Neither establishes native FontLab acceptance.

docs.title: Write boundaries and acceptance
docs.text:
History helpers preflight before mutation, initialize history, mutate, stamp, notify once and read back. retain= enrolls removed component objects with deep history. Failures after history starts raise PartialWriteError with Undo guidance; that guidance is not a guarantee of complete recovery.

Rename, Unicode and geometry edits refuse automatic-layer owners and automatic composite bases; explicit consent can allow supported base edits. Metadata edits refuse automatic-layer owners. Writers disclose queued ids and the possible modification-date changes (FontLab issue 8537); history.commit defaults to settled=False and always captures the queue once before writing. Its result supports result["pending_updates"] and result["pending_note"] (empty when no ids). Writers carry both fields to their results; panels append the stored note with edit_guards.append_note. Legacy scalar writers can fill a disclosure output dictionary or print the disclosure for console use. Use edit_guards.pending_updates(native: Any = None) -> tuple[int, ...] before a write and pending_note(ids: Sequence[int]) -> str in its status. require_settled remains an explicit opt-in refusal. history.commit, glyph_creation.create_glyphs and the eight App writers that notify directly call edit_guards.require_history_scope: with a Glyph window as the active canvas they refuse ("Switch to the Font window first…") unless every owner glyph (matched by font id and glyph name) is in that canvas and no glyph is new (FontLab issue 8573). Glyport and Fontport host notifiers are not guarded yet. Never notify an automatic layer, clear the queue or normalise unrelated dates. Existing-anchor moves to (0, 0) are refused because of a measured Redo defect. Clones must retain raw node flags, names and shape notes.

Font-level master writes use font_history.commit_masters(package, title, {master: MasterEdit(save, write, read, verify, restore)}). It refuses off the GUI thread and unless a Font window of the font is active (no Glyph window canvas; text "Activate the Font window before editing font masters."). It calls checkInitHistoryState(0) on the package and mastersContainer(), writes and reads back each master after setMaster(name, False), restores the original master and sends ONE notifyChangesApplied(title, [package, container], False). The result has values, pending_updates and pending_note. Unlike history.commit, a failure before the notification (also an interrupt, which is then re-raised) restores every written master and the original master and notifies nothing: RolledBackError (a ValueError) when the restore holds, UnrestoredError (a PartialWriteError with no Undo advice) when it does not or when the notification fails. Callers: master_metrics.write_master_metrics(package, {master: {field: value}}, title) for ascender, descender, xHeight, capsHeight and lineGap (capHeight is an alias of capsHeight; unknown fields and non-finite values are refused; double read-back tolerance 1e-9), and zone_native.backend(), the production zone_editor.Backend (Font Info's convertZonesToGuidelines + updateZonesFromGuidelines; the thread and Font-window guards run before any master switch; empty or repeated names and zero-width rows of the other kind raise zone_native.RowRefusal, and Editor.add names new rows as FontLab does (T: 500, T: 500.1); a zone rollback re-creates the zone guides with new ids and says so; a read-back gap after the commit raises history.unstored_error; it does not use the held serializer, fl#8554). The Alignment Zones panel stays usable after a RowRefusal or RolledBackError and locks after a stale source, UnrestoredError or a read-back gap. Known FontLab defect: after Undo or Redo of such a step, both masters show only the zone guidelines, not the six font-metric guidelines, until updateFontMetrics() runs or the font is reopened; the saved file is correct (9.0.9790, fl#8574). select_glyphs and master_switcher.switch call no UpdateAll(): it queued glyph ids and changed nothing visible.

Glyph creation uses fontpr.set_glyph(create=True) and checks the created result; existing names are refused before the call. Components for a new glyph travel in its creation data. Adding components to existing layers requires a qualified plain component prototype. Creation can use multiple native steps; do not promise one Undo for the whole workflow. Unmeasured automatic-layer rebuilding stays guarded.

Earlier releases have bounded native receipts in CHANGELOG. Those receipts do not qualify later shared writers or the full migration. Zone serializer ABI/payload preservation remains open; the route-A zone and metrics writers have no native receipt yet. Current text, NUL/IME, printer/OS, cache/history, font preservation and UI lifecycle holds are listed in TODO. Native proof requires installed artifacts in owned FontLab fixtures, exact source hashes, complete state comparison, real controls, Undo/Redo and saved reopening for writers. Source and standalone Qt checks do not qualify native behavior.

docs.title: Documentation builds
docs.text: Use a separate Python 3.13 environment with the exact hash-locked src_docs/requirements.txt; run sh src_docs/build.sh and python -m unittest discover -s tests_docs -v. ProperDocs and MaterialX generate the site with light fltheme26 and local search. The every-main workflow builds source X and independently qualifies generated child Y using X’s epoch and source identity; unexpected tracked, ignored or untracked output and concurrent changes refuse publication. This is a generated-docs commit pipeline only. Private Pages configuration, requests and deployment remain owner-held.

docs.title: Preserved qualification boundaries
docs.text: The complete runtime reference retains CurrentGlyph, editor, writer, Undo/Redo and native limitations. The background tools guide retains the N86 HOLD and N92 rich-copy source-review blocker; all three workflows remain INCOMPLETE. Issue 123 remains paused and the zone/master lane remains reserved. The future Issue 210 architecture is not a supported current import. Ordinary source, sdist, complete-source harness, installed wheel, native behavior and publication are separate evidence surfaces.

docs.title: API map
docs.text:
The module and domain map lists every App module, its public names and purpose. Additive lazy facades give the main capabilities shorter import paths without loading PythonQt when the facade itself is imported:

from fly.ap.objects import FontLab, current_package
from fly.ap.ui.actions import Action, ActionDisabledError
from fly.ap.ui.canvas import EditorPainters
from fly.ap.ui.dialogs import run_standard_message_box
from fly.ap.menus import OwnedMenus
from fly.ap.signals import track_connection
from fly.ap.qtsafe_api import qt_list

The other facades are fontlabapp.ui.panels, .widgets, .windows, fontlabapp.ui, fontlabapp.shortcuts and fontlabapp.qtsafe_api. Accessing native objects still requires FontLab. The legacy fontlabapp.actions package attribute remains the live host action tree; the facade lives at fontlabapp.ui.actions. The Qt helper facade uses qtsafe_api so its path cannot differ from the existing lazy fontlabapp.Qt name only by case.

Case Coverage provides the original four report controls, complete detached case diagnostics and an explicit existing-view chooser when inactive views are ambiguous. GlyphData metadata is supplied by the Scriptmix caller. Exact native text-block binding and proof usability remain unqualified; a capability refusal is not native acceptance.

docs.title: UI and drawing
docs.text:
FontLab() or Application.control reads fonts, glyphs, metrics and live views; it also exposes native open/new/save/close and tool calls. Tool results and errors retain their JSON form. Raw wrapper reads can produce different Python objects; compare native IDs. output() reads Output without clearing it.

create_panel, create_dialog and create_widget in fontlabapp.qt.widgets build owned UI under MainWindow. Keep handles alive; close them when finished, and retry Close if it returns False or raises. Context exit removes owned controls and overlays. It preserves user views and fonts. Failed factory cleanup exposes both errors and its exact recovery owner. Floating docks and plugin tools request priority. See window recovery for six standalone experiments; native acceptance remains separate.

fontlabapp.qt.views.Drawing paints one widget. Glyph overlays accept pixel or canvas coordinates; canvas coordinates are not implicit glyph-local coordinates. fontlabapp.qt.painting.editor.EditorPainters registers after-native-layer callbacks across visible glyph windows, with affine mapping and active/inactive layer filters. Before-native-layer painting is refused. fontlabapp.qt.menus.OwnedMenus owns actions and tool windows; removal inside its own connected slots is deferred until dispatch returns. Other slots must queue their own teardown. _defer(fn, first=True) queues prerequisite cleanup before pending teardown.

fontlabapp.qt.safe.qt_list converts widget lists with cyclic GC disabled on the GUI thread. fontlabapp.qt.safe.main_window raises MainWindowNotFound. fontlabapp.qt.dialogs executes owned input/file/message dialogs and releases them on exit. Caller adapters retain button, conversion and cancel policy. The extracted painter/menu/dialog workflows still need native acceptance. Offline tests do not establish PythonQt safety.

fontlabapp.qt.dialogs.run_standard_message_box(qt, parent, title, text, icon, buttons, default_button=None) runs an owned priority dialog with static warning/question semantics. Pass "Warning" or "Question" for the icon; the title and primary text stay separate. It preserves standard-button results, explicit No defaults and automatic defaults, and deletes the box on every exit.

fontlabapp.fontui also holds the editors for FontParts-style fonts: font_info_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None), groups_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None), kerning_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None), transform_editor(font, name=None, parent=None, on_change=None) (a detached affine glyph transform), batch_panel(recipe, parent=None, on_finish=None, python=None) (a recipe over source UFOs) and glyph_sequence(font, parent=None, on_select=None) (text or slash-separated glyph names). They validate and apply data with Fontport, so install it with pip install "fontlab-fontlabapp[fontport]"; without it a factory raises ImportError that names the extra. Importing fontlabapp.fontui loads neither PythonQt nor an editor module. Batch work runs in a separate Python 3.11+ that has fontlab-fontport: pass python= or set FONTLABAPP_BATCH_PYTHON. The transform example connects preview and batch. Fontport has no UI (issue 201); these editors lived in fontlab_fontport.ui for one release. Moved editor interaction still needs native acceptance.

The external native UI example uses fontlab-remopy in ordinary external Python to create a native panel, modeless dialog and removable Preview drawing. Install App inside FontLab first; --typerig also needs TypeRig in FontLab. From this source checkout or an extracted sdist, run python examples/native_ui.py --seconds 5 with Remopy installed in the external interpreter. It retains its handles across calls, waits outside the UI thread and removes only its own resources in finally. The example retains its Fontlab Ltd proprietary licence; it is included in the sdist, separate from the installed App runtime. Native requalification against the current combined cohort remains pending.

See drawing, font browser, features, native smoke, Text Holder, Find Files, Character Map, Raise Ascender and kerning proofs.

from fly.ap.qt.safe import qt_list

docs.title: Migration from flat module names (issue 205)
docs.text:
All 382 reviewed old module names remain importable through fontlabapp._legacy. Old imports such as fontlabapp.qtsafe, from fontlabapp import qtsafe, fly.ap.qtsafe and importlib.import_module("fontlabapp.qtsafe") resolve to the same module object as fontlabapp.qt.safe. Existing monkeypatch targets therefore affect the canonical implementation. New code should use the new domain paths.

The six old names anchors, components, guides, hints, masters and proof also name domain packages. Their packages lazily expose the moved implementation's attributes and forward model writes and deletions, including private monkeypatch targets and patch undo. Each model is a separate normal module with its canonical name, file and import metadata. The packages retain their own children, metadata and resource access. No child implementation or PythonQt module is loaded just by importing a domain package. Root public exports remain in place; fontlabapp.fontui also received the Fontport editors and active-font feature helpers in 1.2.0. application, hotkey and utils, including their old child module names, are aliases under core.

The Vanilla tombstone is importable for alias identity, but requesting VanillaSession still raises its Glyport migration error and imports no peer.

The retained stdlib-only migration tool and reviewed mapping document the historical one-off migration that produced this layout. They are migration evidence, not a maintenance command to rerun on the current source tree.

docs.title: Moved in 1.2.0
docs.text:
App never imports Glyport and imports Fontport only inside fontlabapp.fontui, behind the fontport extra. FontLab editors and active-font feature helpers belong in App. Fontport owns DesignSpace/UFO/fontParts and its FontLab backend. Install fontlab-fontlabapp[fontport] for these editors; native operations still need FontLab's PythonQt and existing event loop.

Old Current home Compatibility fontlabapp.vanilla.VanillaSession / fontlabapp.core.legacy.vanilla.VanillaSession fontlab_glyport.ui.session.VanillaSession Session access/from-import raises ImportError; module imports remain available fontlab_fontport.ui factories/modules fontlabapp.fontui matching names Old access raises ImportError with the new home fontlab_fontport.feature_blocks fontlabapp.fontui.feature_blocks Deprecated lazy forwarder; Fontport's fontlab extra supplies App fontlabapp.core.scripting.read_feature_blocks, fontlabapp.core.scripting.write_feature_blocks fontlabapp.fontui.feature_blocks Restored lazy function wrappers extras [fontedit], [fontsequence] [fontport] Install the current extra fontlabapp._qtsafe fontlabapp.qt.safe Old import raises ModuleNotFoundError text match on "main window not found" fontlabapp.qt.safe.MainWindowNotFound Same text and RuntimeError base

Example: from fontlab_fontport.ui import kerning_editor becomes from fly.ap.fontui import kerning_editor; import fontlab_fontport.ui.kerning becomes import fly.ap.fontui.kerning.

The lazy factories on fontlabapp.fontui preserve their signatures:

Factory Purpose font_info_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None) Stage font information groups_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None) Edit groups kerning_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None) Inspect/edit kerning transform_editor(font, name=None, parent=None, on_change=None) Preview affine glyph transforms batch_panel(recipe, parent=None, on_finish=None, python=None) Run a UFO recipe in a child interpreter glyph_sequence(font, parent=None, on_select=None) Preview placed glyph sequences

Importing the facade loads neither Qt nor Fontport. Call a factory inside FontLab, retain the handle, and call close() when finished. Batch requires an installed Python 3.11+ with Fontport; pass python= or set FONTLABAPP_BATCH_PYTHON. See the transform example. fontui.feature_blocks.read_feature_blocks(package) reads ordered VFJ source; write_feature_blocks(package, expected, updated, references=..., undo_name=...) checks the active font, source snapshot and glyph references, restores the master, and returns {"changed": 0 or 1}. Unexpected host failures can leave partial changes.

docs.title: Demo scripts
docs.text:
Scripts/<Category>/<Tool> Demo.py holds small GUI demos of the App modules, one menu entry each (146 in 15 categories). install.vfpy copies them into FontLab's Scripts menu; the Demo.py suffix keeps them apart from Fly's Scriptmix scripts when both are installed. Demos import App through fly.ap and keep native imports lazy inside main(). They write nothing by themselves: no font, selection, history, preference, Output or clipboard, and no menu action is triggered. The exceptions start with your own click: the Copy buttons of Glyph Map and Common Glyphs write the clipboard; Proof Tabs, Kerning Proofs and Text Filter open a text tab only after you confirm or tick a box; Image Viewer's Print can write a PDF to a path you pick; and Text Holder, Text Filter and Image Viewer keep files in fixed fontlabapp-demos/<demo> folders under the system temp directory. Each script's Safety paragraph gives the details. tests/test_demo_scripts.py checks every file's layout, header and Fly imports by AST; tests/_demo_support.py runs a demo offline under stubbed natives. Four demos show core features in use rather than by name: Shim Generator (core.shimgen), Native Tabs (core.native_tabs), History Preflight (core.history) and Owned Lifetime (core.completion and the fontlabapp.ui factories); the last one adds a small panel to the main window (it may float) and removes it on close. Native FontLab acceptance of the demos is pending. tests/test_demo_scripts_coverage.py fails when a fontlabapp.<domain>.<feature> module has no demo naming it.

Named but not run, and why. The coverage test counts a module that a demo names, so some are named or summarised without running, for these reasons:

  • components.panel, contours.panel, anchors.panel and guides.rewrite hold the writer panels of the component, contour, anchor and guide scripts, and contours.copy and anchors.edit copy contours and run point transactions. Their buttons change glyphs, so Component Writers, Contour Panels, Anchor Plans and Guide Plans compute the plans on made-up data and only name the panels.
  • core.hotkey: its macOS HotkeyManager creates a session-wide Quartz event tap and needs the Accessibility permission, and on Windows it raises NotImplementedError. A demo would register global hotkeys, so Signals And Hotkeys only reports whether the backend can load.
  • core.legacy: examples launches relocated scripts with runpy, and vanilla is a tombstone that raises ImportError naming Glyport. Core Utilities shows their summaries.
  • fontlabapp.ui.actions, canvas, dialogs, panels, widgets and windows re-export objects of qt and core. Owned Lifetime runs create_widget, create_panel and create_dialog through that facade; the rest need live native objects or act on FontLab (actions triggers menu items, canvas registers painters on the glyph editor, windows wraps native glyph and preview windows), so Toolkit Reference lists their __all__ only.

docs.title: Object JSON (FontLab 9.1)
docs.text: FontLab 9.1 writes glyphs, layers, elements and contours as object JSON ("dataType": "com.fontlab.objects") and reads that JSON back into detached objects. fontlabapp.objects.json_data parses and edits the JSON in plain Python (Envelope, describe, rename_glyphs, unique_glyph_names, filter_layers, set_advance_width) and wraps the native calls (export, decode, clipboard and file helpers). paste_glyphs creates new glyphs through create_glyphs (each glyph its own Undo step, the outlines one more), with names made unique; a Unicode value already in the font or earlier in the paste is dropped with a note, and a name that may make FontLab rebuild automatic glyphs is skipped unless allow_rebuild=True. If the write stops part way, the scripts report what exists and point to Edit > Undo; paste_shapes adds shapes or contours to one layer as one Undo step. decode always hands FontLab a QByteArray: Python bytes crash FontLab 9.1.9812. On FontLab 9.0 the Objects scripts say they need 9.1 and change nothing.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use Python 3.11 arm64. The test extra supplies pytest, Markdown/PyMdown, ufoLib2, fontParts, fontTools and PySide6-Essentials. PySide6 is an offline test binding; it does not replace FontLab's PythonQt.

The full suite also needs fontlab-fly installed with its target packages. Adding Fly's source directory to PYTHONPATH alone is insufficient. The commands under Testing install the local App, Fontport and Glyport checkouts with their dependencies into a prepared virtual environment, and Fly with --no-deps: Fly's own target packages (Echopy, PythonQtSide) are not published on a package index. Sibling checkouts must exist at ../fontlab-fly, ../fontlab-fontport and ../fontlab-glyport.

Editable installation into FontLab is owner-managed. Do not install or uninstall packages in FontLab's Python site-packages from a development or test session. Use a reviewed installed artifact and verify its import origin for native tests. This branch is development source; a historical tag or candidate floor does not prove that its current API is available from a package index.

Optional extras:

Extra Purpose markdown Python-Markdown and PyMdown conversion hotkeys macOS Quartz hooks; needs existing Accessibility permission unicode Extended Unicode data through unicodedata2 fontui fontTools for outline and browser helpers fontport fontlab-fontport and its fontParts/UFO stack, which the six FontParts editors and feature helpers in fontlabapp.fontui need

Windows global hotkeys are not implemented. macOS global capture remains unverified. No feature compiler is supplied.

docs.title: Use inside FontLab
docs.text:
User scripts, examples and the optional startup block require FontLab Fly 1.3.0 or later in the same interpreter. Libraries retain canonical provider imports without a mandatory Fly dependency.

The source installer copies Scripts and writes App's owned startup block, but does not install or check Fly. Install Fly and its matching providers separately in the same interpreter before running these consumers or relying on plugin startup. A missing Fly import makes the startup block print FontLab plugins startup: and skip activation.

Read application state without opening or saving PrefLib:

from fly.ap import Application
app = Application(with_ui=True, with_preflib=False)
print(app.versions.app_version)
print(app.control.current_font())

fontlabapp.app creates the legacy context lazily. Explicit Application() initializes UI and PrefLib by default. PrefLib preserves attribute dictionaries and JSON; malformed or non-object JSON fails before saving.

Scripts use the Fly namespace. Keep the module import form:

import fly.ap.core.scripting as scripting
import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history

package = scripting.current_package()
print(scripting.font_id(package))  # fontpr uses fgId, not package.id

Outside FontLab, import a pure submodule directly:

from fly.ap.core.utils import deepmerge, slugify
from fly.ap.contours.affine import apply, IDENTITY
print(apply(IDENTITY, 20, 30))

Real subpackages and legacy aliases resolve before native API names, so from fly.ap import core also works outside FontLab. Prefer explicit domain paths in new code. host.menu.font.find("kern")
host.panels.preview.show()
host.menu.view.measurements.tension.set_checked(True)

Lookups resolve current QAction objects after menu rebuilds. Reading an attribute, dir or repr does not trigger an action. Disabled actions raise ActionDisabledError. Font Map has no exposed panel state.

docs.title: Plugmix
docs.text:
fontlabapp.plugmix adds native FontLab 9 plugins: reporter overlays, an undoable filter, a dockable palette, a native tool and a General menu command. It uses PythonQt and native per-canvas painters when available, with fontlabapp.qt.painting.editor.EditorPainters on older builds. It imports no PySide2 and no Glyphs emulation. Importing it does not need FontLab.

Install it once per FontLab session from your own initScript.py:

Install Fly and its matching providers separately in the same interpreter before plugin startup; Fly 1.3.0 or later is required. App's source installer writes its startup block without installing or checking Fly. If Fly is missing, the generated block prints FontLab plugins startup: and skips activation.

try:
    from fly.ap.plugmix import install; install()
except Exception as error: print(f"Plugmix startup: {error}")

The Scripts in fontlab-python-plugmix (Install Plugmix Menu, Duplicate Anchor Rings) call the same install(). It appends a View > Reporters submenu with one checkable action per reporter, a separator and Hide All (turns every reporter off), adds Plugmix: Delete Small Paths… to the Glyph menu, Plugmix: Step and Repeat Panel and Plugmix: Tool Smart Select to the Window menu, and Plugmix: Zoom to Selection to the View menu. Choices are saved in ~/Library/Application Support/FontLab/FontLab 9/Data/fontlab-plugmix.json (enabled, enabled_filters, enabled_palettes, enabled_tools, enabled_general, last-used params). install(config_dir=...) selects another directory. fontlabapp.plugmix.boot.uninstall() removes actions, overlays and panels and keeps the saved choices. Filters, tools and General plugins start enabled; palettes start hidden. No font data is written.

Kind Plugin Behaviour Filter Delete Small Paths Deletes closed contours whose flattened path or bounds area is below the threshold (default 400 units²) in selected glyphs of the current master, in one geometry Undo step. Skips shared or transformed outlines and automatic layers. Palette Step and Repeat Duplicates selected contours of the active glyph count more times, each shifted by another (dx, dy), in one geometry Undo step. Refuses shared or transformed outlines and two zero offsets. Tool Smart Select Drag a rectangle to select whole contours touched by any node; Shift toggles. Selection only; it never changes outlines. General Zoom to Selection Fits the active glyph's selected nodes in the canvas with a margin.

Native Tool activation, drag mapping, overlay lifetime, General actions and font events were verified in FontLab 9. Shortcut handling and keyboard cursor mapping were later corrected from native findings and still need an in-app recheck. The palette refresh key reads the glyph modification timestamp and node selection; confirm that edits outside Plugmix advance that timestamp in your build.

Write a reporter by subclassing fontlabapp.plugmix.Reporter with a unique name, a title and a pure compute(snapshot) that returns Mark objects (ring, line, polyline, polygon, text) in glyph units; pixel sizes are view pixels. Set layer = "background" to paint under the glyph layer. An error raised by compute or requested_glyphs goes to the error sink once per reporter and message until Plugmix is uninstalled. Every snapshot also carries identity (name, Unicodes, raw mark, mark RGB, export flag) and view.px_per_unit; either is None when it cannot be read, and the read error goes to the plugin error sink once. Mark RGB uses HSL lightness 0.65, so it differs slightly from FontLab's flag swatches (inferred, unverified natively). Offline coverage only. Opt-in class flags add costlier data: needs_components gives components (base name, transform and decomposed base contours, nested up to 8 levels), needs_background gives background (the mask's contours, () when empty, None when there is none), and needs_masters gives masters (each master's contours, anchors, advance and a compatible flag that compares contour count, node count per contour and on/off-curve pattern with the shown layer, ignoring components and open/closed state). Components and masters are cached per glyph revision and shared by all reporters; components also re-check their base glyphs. Master outlines may lag until the foreground glyph's lastModified moves, which is unverified natively. The background is read on every paint. An empty component layer means the master that owns the shown layer. Metrics also come from that master. Zones and the italic angle need a master switch to read, so when the shown layer belongs to another master the zones are empty and the italic slant is the current master's. Skipped components and failed reads go to the error sink once. Offline coverage only. needs_kerning gives kerning_groups (the classes used when the glyph is a pair's first member, left, and second member, right, with their members), read on every paint because a class edit may not move the glyph's timestamp. Override requested_glyphs(identity, kerning_groups=None) to name up to 32 other glyphs; others maps each one that exists to its own unselected contours (components skipped), cached per requested glyph's revision. Both use the master that owns the shown layer. needs_neighbours gives view.neighbours: the previous and next glyph on the same line as (name, kerning), kerning in font units as displayed (0 when kerning processing is off). Which glyph stores a pair's kerning is inferred, unverified natively. Neighbours need the native canvas painter backend; with EditorPainters, or when the view scale is unusable, they are None. Offline coverage only. needs_mouse gives view.mouse, the cursor in the glyph's own units (canvas.mousePosition() mapped back through the glyph and text-block transforms), or None when the map is not invertible. While any enabled reporter asks for it, one event filter watches the active glyph window and flushes (updateScreenRect plus updateViewport) at most once per 16 ms after mouse moves, ending with a flush after the last move. The filter goes when the last such reporter is disabled, when the active canvas changes or closes, and on uninstall(). Only the watched canvas gets a mouse; with EditorPainters it is None. Whether moves reach the filter under every tool is unverified natively. Offline coverage only. Third-party packages publish plugin classes in the fontlabapp.plugmix entry-point group.

docs.title: Current reporter menu ownership
docs.text: View > Reporters uses sorted bare display labels, with a separator and Hide All at the end. Hide All saves the disabled reporter state and resynchronises checkmarks; a failed save retains the previous persisted state. Boot installs this submenu after the other plugin kinds. fontlabapp.qt.menus.OwnedMenus owns the submenu and its action tokens. Removing a submenu removes its owned tokens before Qt deletes their parent, including removal requested during a child callback. Standalone Qt and PythonQt-shaped regression checks cover this lifecycle; current native placement, dispatch and teardown remain unverified.

docs.title: Planned plugin ownership (Issue 210)
docs.text: The fontlabapp.plugmix APIs above are current Issue 209 source. Issue 210 requests framework, scaffolding, discovery, registration and lifecycle under fontlabapp.plugins, with concrete bundles in Plugmix Extensions. Keep existing APIs usable until all callers migrate. Qualify bundle discovery, Reporters palette and View > Reporters, toolbar and Tools > Tool, Window > Panels, and a preservation-safe initScript.py installer hook. The target path is not yet a supported current import.

docs.title: Feature source and proof candidate
docs.text:
Feature Source and Proof is available through fontlabapp.fontui.feature_proof.show(font, parent=None). It keeps the ordinary code view, refuses unsupported input before selection loss, and quarantines opaque document changes until explicit Revert. Accepted source Apply refreshes the independent Unicode/kerning sequence once; it does not compile or shape OpenType features. The window captures one borrowed font. External changes retain dirty drafts with a warning; explicit Apply can overwrite newer source. Refresh proof retries only the view. Original paragraph separators are inspect-only. Focused checks confirm exact UFO source preservation through the backend and editor for CR, CRLF, mixed endings and absent final newlines, including untouched siblings; duplicate feature tags are inspect-only. This candidate is not yet source-qualified; complete Fontport/App/fresh Scriptmix suites and ordinary artifact/native history/reopen qualification remain pending. Native PythonQt/FontLab, full literal paragraph-separator editing and broader clipboard routes remain unqualified.

fontlabapp.fontui.feature_source.create_source_input is the binding-injected source boundary used by the existing feature editor; FeatureState remains the owner of blocks and line endings. The new demo exercises this boundary through the actual source/proof window.

The optional fontlabapp.fontui.twindow_host.Host protocol supplies text and owned follow notifications for TMetrics and TGlyph. FontLabHost binds one font and one exact Glyph-window text block; Fontport retains explicit-layer outline and metric transactions. Native round-trip qualification is pending.

docs.title: Pedro background tools
docs.text:
Scale takes a finite percentage (including fractions and negatives), multiplies background own path nodes about the origin, and leaves components untouched. Shift takes a finite x offset, moves every background own path node and component position, and preserves y and the component linear transform. Both process selected layers in order; a repeated layer receives the operation again. The dialog captures selection when Apply is pressed and closes on success. Invalid input leaves the field and dialog open for correction.

Selection to All the Backgrounds runs immediately. It uses only the first selected layer, copies each whole path whose every node is selected (including an empty contour), and excludes components. It replaces that layer background and the selected-master background of every glyph in font order. The first layer may be auxiliary, so its background is an additional destination. No selected whole paths means clear all those backgrounds. Later selected layers are not read. Existing mask custom metadata, identity, width and inherited mark state remain attached while old shapes, anchors and nonhint guides are replaced.

FontLab mapping uses native mask layers. Foreign, automatic or hint-bearing replacement masks and missing selected-master foregrounds diagnose the whole operation before history; no subset is reported as success. Existing background metadata remains in place. Copies preserve notes, raw node states, open/closed and cubic/quadratic topology. Originals are never executed or packaged.

A changed selection, document, master, complete destination inventory or background content refuses before mutation. Copies are staged before history. Attachment failures attempt scoped geometry recovery, retain all errors and poison the adapter; late history/cache failures may retain changes. Reopen only after reviewing native history. No global Undo, UpdateAll, preference writer, Output clearing or event pump is used. Paint updates restore their prior state.

This is a source and installed-artifact candidate. Native acceptance is pending: owned full-font/cache/dependency preservation, successive different-glyph edits, Apply/Undo/Redo/save/reopen and actual Qt lifecycle. No native calls were made.

N86 HOLD — independent N92 source review found a core rich-copy blocker. FontLab ShapeImpl::assignStyle calls the source-mutating getPenParameters and copies effective content lock into the raw destination lock. cloneCustom uses that route. Current Python bindings cannot observe/restore those private fields. All three workflows remain INCOMPLETE and unqualified for integration despite passing ordinary offline artifacts. No native calls, canonical apply or push. Exact source pins, unapplied native fix direction and before-history source counterexamples are retained in background-family-z33 and independent N92.

docs.title: FontLab application utilities
docs.text:
fontlab-fontlabapp provides the fontlabapp package: shared FontLab application, UI, drawing, reporting and guarded editing helpers. It supplies reusable mechanics for Fly, Fontport, Glyport and FontLab scripts. Python 3.11 arm64 is the host target. The package declares Python >=3.11 and requires fontlab-python-pens>=1.0.0. Fontport remains optional through the fontport extra.

The host-free smallcap_consistency engine reports exporting case counts, missing and orphan smallcaps, legacy capital/lowercase coverage and two-sided kerning-group differences. The legacy_lowercase_without_smallcaps section independently requires an exporting .sc glyph even when modern .smcp coverage passes. smallcap_capture.current_report() lazily captures the current font and master within a shared three-second budget. Export scope is explicitly the public.skipExportGlyphs compatibility policy; unknown mappings and ambiguous groups are disclosed. Native qualification remains pending.

Pure utility modules load outside FontLab. Native operations require FontLab's fontlab, FL, fontgate, fontpr and PythonQt APIs as used by each operation. Native modules and panels load on demand. General UI belongs here; FontParts/UFO adapters belong in Fontport; Glyphs.app compatibility belongs in Glyport. App never imports Glyport. Optional Fontport imports are confined to fontui; base App still installs without Fontport. Scriptmix scripts and App's own Scripts/ access App through fly.ap.

docs.title: API map
docs.text:
The module and domain map lists every App module, its public names and purpose. Additive lazy facades give the main capabilities shorter import paths without loading PythonQt when the facade itself is imported:

from fly.ap.objects import FontLab, current_package
from fly.ap.ui.actions import Action, ActionDisabledError
from fly.ap.ui.canvas import EditorPainters
from fly.ap.ui.dialogs import run_standard_message_box
from fly.ap.menus import OwnedMenus
from fly.ap.signals import track_connection
from fly.ap.qtsafe_api import qt_list

The other facades are fontlabapp.ui.panels, .widgets, .windows, fontlabapp.ui, fontlabapp.shortcuts and fontlabapp.qtsafe_api. Accessing native objects still requires FontLab. The legacy fontlabapp.actions package attribute remains the live host action tree; the facade lives at fontlabapp.ui.actions. The Qt helper facade uses qtsafe_api so its path cannot differ from the existing lazy fontlabapp.Qt name only by case.

Case Coverage provides the original four report controls, complete detached case diagnostics and an explicit existing-view chooser when inactive views are ambiguous. GlyphData metadata is supplied by the Scriptmix caller. Exact native text-block binding and proof usability remain unqualified; a capability refusal is not native acceptance.

docs.title: Original Node Duplicator actions
docs.text:
node_duplicator_native.duplicate_selected_nodes(mode) is the guarded immediate entry point. Choose mode "current", "all" or "handles" for the three source policies. Current and handles operate on the first selected layer. All broadcasts its selected on-curve indices to every stored foreground layer of each selected parent occurrence, retaining duplicate layer names and repeated parents. Handles adds two fresh coincident controls and a copied curve endpoint. The separate Scriptmix Node Duplicator panel retains its per-glyph reference/preview behavior.

Copies restore named native metadata and fractional positions; existing node and captured layer/shape metadata are checked. Shared owners, automatic dependants, hinted topology and unrepresentable control cases are refused. Queue ids are disclosed without clearing them. A partial failure carries exact owned recovery handles and whether its history notification returned; this does not prove actual Undo/Redo or saved-font preservation. Do not blindly retry it. The full native/four-font/window-priority/lifetime workflow still needs acceptance.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use Python 3.11 arm64. The test extra supplies pytest, Markdown/PyMdown, ufoLib2, fontParts, fontTools and PySide6-Essentials. PySide6 is an offline test binding; it does not replace FontLab's PythonQt.

The full suite also needs fontlab-fly installed with its target packages. Adding Fly's source directory to PYTHONPATH alone is insufficient. The commands under Testing install the local App, Fontport and Glyport checkouts with their dependencies into a prepared virtual environment, and Fly with --no-deps: Fly's own target packages (Echopy, PythonQtSide) are not published on a package index. Sibling checkouts must exist at ../fontlab-fly, ../fontlab-fontport and ../fontlab-glyport.

Editable installation into FontLab is owner-managed. Do not install or uninstall packages in FontLab's Python site-packages from a development or test session. Use a reviewed installed artifact and verify its import origin for native tests. This branch is development source; a historical tag or candidate floor does not prove that its current API is available from a package index.

Optional extras:

Extra Purpose markdown Python-Markdown and PyMdown conversion hotkeys macOS Quartz hooks; needs existing Accessibility permission unicode Extended Unicode data through unicodedata2 fontui fontTools for outline and browser helpers fontport fontlab-fontport and its fontParts/UFO stack, which the six FontParts editors and feature helpers in fontlabapp.fontui need

Windows global hotkeys are not implemented. macOS global capture remains unverified. No feature compiler is supplied.

docs.title: Use inside FontLab
docs.text:
Read application state without opening or saving PrefLib:

from fly.ap import Application
app = Application(with_ui=True, with_preflib=False)
print(app.versions.app_version)
print(app.control.current_font())

fontlabapp.app creates the legacy context lazily. Explicit Application() initializes UI and PrefLib by default. PrefLib preserves attribute dictionaries and JSON; malformed or non-object JSON fails before saving.

Scripts use the Fly namespace. Keep the module import form:

import fly.ap.core.scripting as scripting
import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history

package = scripting.current_package()
print(scripting.font_id(package))  # fontpr uses fgId, not package.id

Outside FontLab, import a pure submodule directly:

from fly.ap.core.utils import deepmerge, slugify
from fly.ap.contours.affine import apply, IDENTITY
print(apply(IDENTITY, 20, 30))

Real subpackages and legacy aliases resolve before native API names, so from fly.ap import core also works outside FontLab. Prefer explicit domain paths in new code. Outside FontLab, unknown names raise AttributeError on attribute access or ImportError on from-import. Explicit native names still raise a host-required RuntimeError outside FontLab.

Read and trigger native menus with fontlabapp.core.host:

from fly.ap.core import host
host.menu.font.find("kern")
host.panels.preview.show()
host.menu.view.measurements.tension.set_checked(True)

Lookups resolve current QAction objects after menu rebuilds. Reading an attribute, dir or repr does not trigger an action. Disabled actions raise ActionDisabledError. Font Map has no exposed panel state.

docs.title: UI and drawing
docs.text:
FontLab() or Application.control reads fonts, glyphs, metrics and live views; it also exposes native open/new/save/close and tool calls. Tool results and errors retain their JSON form. Raw wrapper reads can produce different Python objects; compare native IDs. output() reads Output without clearing it.

create_panel, create_dialog and create_widget in fontlabapp.qt.widgets build owned UI under MainWindow. Keep handles alive; close them when finished, and retry Close if it returns False or raises. Context exit removes owned controls and overlays. It preserves user views and fonts. Failed factory cleanup exposes both errors and its exact recovery owner. Floating docks and plugin tools request priority. See window recovery for six standalone experiments; native acceptance remains separate.

fontlabapp.qt.views.Drawing paints one widget. Glyph overlays accept pixel or canvas coordinates; canvas coordinates are not implicit glyph-local coordinates. fontlabapp.qt.painting.editor.EditorPainters registers after-native-layer callbacks across visible glyph windows, with affine mapping and active/inactive layer filters. Before-native-layer painting is refused. fontlabapp.qt.menus.OwnedMenus owns actions and tool windows; removal inside its own connected slots is deferred until dispatch returns. Other slots must queue their own teardown. _defer(fn, first=True) queues prerequisite cleanup before pending teardown.

fontlabapp.qt.safe.qt_list converts widget lists with cyclic GC disabled on the GUI thread. fontlabapp.qt.safe.main_window raises MainWindowNotFound. fontlabapp.qt.dialogs executes owned input/file/message dialogs and releases them on exit. Caller adapters retain button, conversion and cancel policy. The extracted painter/menu/dialog workflows still need native acceptance. Offline tests do not establish PythonQt safety.

fontlabapp.qt.dialogs.run_standard_message_box(qt, parent, title, text, icon, buttons, default_button=None) runs an owned priority dialog with static warning/question semantics. Pass "Warning" or "Question" for the icon; the title and primary text stay separate. It preserves standard-button results, explicit No defaults and automatic defaults, and deletes the box on every exit.

fontlabapp.fontui also holds the editors for FontParts-style fonts: font_info_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None), groups_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None), kerning_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None), transform_editor(font, name=None, parent=None, on_change=None) (a detached affine glyph transform), batch_panel(recipe, parent=None, on_finish=None, python=None) (a recipe over source UFOs) and glyph_sequence(font, parent=None, on_select=None) (text or slash-separated glyph names). They validate and apply data with Fontport, so install it with pip install "fontlab-fontlabapp[fontport]"; without it a factory raises ImportError that names the extra. Importing fontlabapp.fontui loads neither PythonQt nor an editor module. Batch work runs in a separate Python 3.11+ that has fontlab-fontport: pass python= or set FONTLABAPP_BATCH_PYTHON. The transform example connects preview and batch. Fontport has no UI (issue 201); these editors lived in fontlab_fontport.ui for one release. Moved editor interaction still needs native acceptance.

The external native UI example uses fontlab-remopy in ordinary external Python to create a native panel, modeless dialog and removable Preview drawing. Install App inside FontLab first; --typerig also needs TypeRig in FontLab. From this source checkout or an extracted sdist, run python examples/native_ui.py --seconds 5 with Remopy installed in the external interpreter. It retains its handles across calls, waits outside the UI thread and removes only its own resources in finally. The example retains its Fontlab Ltd proprietary licence; it is included in the sdist, separate from the installed App runtime. Native requalification against the current combined cohort remains pending.

See drawing, font browser, features, native smoke, Text Holder, Find Files, Character Map, Raise Ascender and kerning proofs.

docs.title: Migration from flat module names (issue 205)
docs.text:
All 382 reviewed old module names remain importable through fontlabapp._legacy. Old imports such as fontlabapp.qtsafe, from fontlabapp import qtsafe, fly.ap.qtsafe and importlib.import_module("fontlabapp.qtsafe") resolve to the same module object as fontlabapp.qt.safe. Existing monkeypatch targets therefore affect the canonical implementation. New code should use the new domain paths.

The six old names anchors, components, guides, hints, masters and proof also name domain packages. Their packages lazily expose the moved implementation's attributes and forward model writes and deletions, including private monkeypatch targets and patch undo. Each model is a separate normal module with its canonical name, file and import metadata. The packages retain their own children, metadata and resource access. No child implementation or PythonQt module is loaded just by importing a domain package. Root public exports remain in place; fontlabapp.fontui also received the Fontport editors and active-font feature helpers in 1.2.0. application, hotkey and utils, including their old child module names, are aliases under core.

The Vanilla tombstone is importable for alias identity, but requesting VanillaSession still raises its Glyport migration error and imports no peer.

The retained stdlib-only migration tool and reviewed mapping document the historical one-off migration that produced this layout. They are migration evidence, not a maintenance command to rerun on the current source tree.

docs.title: Plugmix
docs.text:
fontlabapp.plugmix adds native FontLab 9 plugins: reporter overlays, an undoable filter, a dockable palette, a native tool and a General menu command. It uses PythonQt and native per-canvas painters when available, with fontlabapp.qt.painting.editor.EditorPainters on older builds. It imports no PySide2 and no Glyphs emulation. Importing it does not need FontLab.

Install it once per FontLab session from your own initScript.py:

Before startup, separately install Fly 1.3.0 or later and its matching providers in the same interpreter; App's source installer does not supply or check Fly.

try:
    from fly.ap.plugins import install; install()
except Exception as error: print(f"Plugmix startup: {error}")

The Scripts in fontlab-python-plugmix (Install Plugmix Menu, Duplicate Anchor Rings) call the same install(). It appends a View > Reporters submenu with one checkable action per reporter, a separator and Hide All (turns every reporter off), adds Plugmix: Delete Small Paths… to the Glyph menu, Plugmix: Step and Repeat Panel and Plugmix: Tool Smart Select to the Window menu, and Plugmix: Zoom to Selection to the View menu. Choices are saved in ~/Library/Application Support/FontLab/FontLab 9/Data/fontlab-plugmix.json (enabled, enabled_filters, enabled_palettes, enabled_tools, enabled_general, last-used params). install(config_dir=...) selects another directory. fontlabapp.plugmix.boot.uninstall() removes actions, overlays and panels and keeps the saved choices. Filters, tools and General plugins start enabled; palettes start hidden. No font data is written.

Kind Plugin Behaviour Filter Delete Small Paths Deletes closed contours whose flattened path or bounds area is below the threshold (default 400 units²) in selected glyphs of the current master, in one geometry Undo step. Skips shared or transformed outlines and automatic layers. Palette Step and Repeat Duplicates selected contours of the active glyph count more times, each shifted by another (dx, dy), in one geometry Undo step. Refuses shared or transformed outlines and two zero offsets. Tool Smart Select Drag a rectangle to select whole contours touched by any node; Shift toggles. Selection only; it never changes outlines. General Zoom to Selection Fits the active glyph's selected nodes in the canvas with a margin.

Native Tool activation, drag mapping, overlay lifetime, General actions and font events were verified in FontLab 9. Shortcut handling and keyboard cursor mapping were later corrected from native findings and still need an in-app recheck. The palette refresh key reads the glyph modification timestamp and node selection; confirm that edits outside Plugmix advance that timestamp in your build.

The original seven reporters, native canvas drawing and all 18 pre-revision reporters were checked in FontLab 9; Glyph Focus and the revised slant and unit grid have offline coverage only. Write a reporter by subclassing fontlabapp.plugmix.Reporter with a unique name, a title and a pure compute(snapshot) that returns Mark objects (ring, line, polyline, polygon, text) in glyph units; pixel sizes are view pixels. Set layer = "background" to paint under the glyph layer. An error raised by compute or requested_glyphs goes to the error sink once per reporter and message until Plugmix is uninstalled. Every snapshot also carries identity (name, Unicodes, raw mark, mark RGB, export flag) and view.px_per_unit; either is None when it cannot be read, and the read error goes to the plugin error sink once. Mark RGB uses HSL lightness 0.65, so it differs slightly from FontLab's flag swatches (inferred, unverified natively). Offline coverage only. Opt-in class flags add costlier data: needs_components gives components (base name, transform and decomposed base contours, nested up to 8 levels), needs_background gives background (the mask's contours, () when empty, None when there is none), and needs_masters gives masters (each master's contours, anchors, advance and a compatible flag that compares contour count, node count per contour and on/off-curve pattern with the shown layer, ignoring components and open/closed state). Components and masters are cached per glyph revision and shared by all reporters; components also re-check their base glyphs. Master outlines may lag until the foreground glyph's lastModified moves, which is unverified natively. The background is read on every paint. An empty component layer means the master that owns the shown layer. Metrics also come from that master. Zones and the italic angle need a master switch to read, so when the shown layer belongs to another master the zones are empty and the italic slant is the current master's. Skipped components and failed reads go to the error sink once. Offline coverage only. needs_kerning gives kerning_groups (the classes used when the glyph is a pair's first member, left, and second member, right, with their members), read on every paint because a class edit may not move the glyph's timestamp. Override requested_glyphs(identity, kerning_groups=None) to name up to 32 other glyphs; others maps each one that exists to its own unselected contours (components skipped), cached per requested glyph's revision. Both use the master that owns the shown layer. needs_neighbours gives view.neighbours: the previous and next glyph on the same line as (name, kerning), kerning in font units as displayed (0 when kerning processing is off). Which glyph stores a pair's kerning is inferred, unverified natively. Neighbours need the native canvas painter backend; with EditorPainters, or when the view scale is unusable, they are None. Offline coverage only. needs_mouse gives view.mouse, the cursor in the glyph's own units (canvas.mousePosition() mapped back through the glyph and text-block transforms), or None when the map is not invertible. While any enabled reporter asks for it, one event filter watches the active glyph window and flushes (updateScreenRect plus updateViewport) at most once per 16 ms after mouse moves, ending with a flush after the last move. The filter goes when the last such reporter is disabled, when the active canvas changes or closes, and on uninstall(). Only the watched canvas gets a mouse; with EditorPainters it is None. Whether moves reach the filter under every tool is unverified natively. Offline coverage only. Third-party packages publish plugin classes in the fontlabapp.plugmix entry-point group.

docs.title: Write boundaries and acceptance
docs.text:
History helpers preflight before mutation, initialize history, mutate, stamp, notify once and read back. retain= enrolls removed component objects with deep history. Failures after history starts raise PartialWriteError with Undo guidance; that guidance is not a guarantee of complete recovery.

Rename, Unicode and geometry edits refuse automatic-layer owners and automatic composite bases; explicit consent can allow supported base edits. Metadata edits refuse automatic-layer owners. Writers disclose queued ids and the possible modification-date changes (FontLab issue 8537); history.commit defaults to settled=False and always captures the queue once before writing. Its result supports result["pending_updates"] and result["pending_note"] (empty when no ids). Writers carry both fields to their results; panels append the stored note with edit_guards.append_note. Legacy scalar writers can fill a disclosure output dictionary or print the disclosure for console use. Use edit_guards.pending_updates(native: Any = None) -> tuple[int, ...] before a write and pending_note(ids: Sequence[int]) -> str in its status. require_settled remains an explicit opt-in refusal. history.commit, glyph_creation.create_glyphs and the eight App writers that notify directly call edit_guards.require_history_scope: with a Glyph window as the active canvas they refuse ("Switch to the Font window first…") unless every owner glyph (matched by font id and glyph name) is in that canvas and no glyph is new (FontLab issue 8573). Glyport and Fontport host notifiers are not guarded yet. Never notify an automatic layer, clear the queue or normalise unrelated dates. Existing-anchor moves to (0, 0) are refused because of a measured Redo defect. Clones must retain raw node flags, names and shape notes.

Font-level master writes use font_history.commit_masters(package, title, {master: MasterEdit(save, write, read, verify, restore)}). It refuses off the GUI thread and unless a Font window of the font is active (no Glyph window canvas; text "Activate the Font window before editing font masters."). It calls checkInitHistoryState(0) on the package and mastersContainer(), writes and reads back each master after setMaster(name, False), restores the original master and sends ONE notifyChangesApplied(title, [package, container], False). The result has values, pending_updates and pending_note. Unlike history.commit, a failure before the notification (also an interrupt, which is then re-raised) restores every written master and the original master and notifies nothing: RolledBackError (a ValueError) when the restore holds, UnrestoredError (a PartialWriteError with no Undo advice) when it does not or when the notification fails. Callers: master_metrics.write_master_metrics(package, {master: {field: value}}, title) for ascender, descender, xHeight, capsHeight and lineGap (capHeight is an alias of capsHeight; unknown fields and non-finite values are refused; double read-back tolerance 1e-9), and zone_native.backend(), the production zone_editor.Backend (Font Info's convertZonesToGuidelines + updateZonesFromGuidelines; the thread and Font-window guards run before any master switch; empty or repeated names and zero-width rows of the other kind raise zone_native.RowRefusal, and Editor.add names new rows as FontLab does (T: 500, T: 500.1); a zone rollback re-creates the zone guides with new ids and says so; a read-back gap after the commit raises history.unstored_error; it does not use the held serializer, fl#8554). The Alignment Zones panel stays usable after a RowRefusal or RolledBackError and locks after a stale source, UnrestoredError or a read-back gap. Known FontLab defect: after Undo or Redo of such a step, both masters show only the zone guidelines, not the six font-metric guidelines, until updateFontMetrics() runs or the font is reopened; the saved file is correct (9.0.9790, fl#8574). select_glyphs and master_switcher.switch call no UpdateAll(): it queued glyph ids and changed nothing visible.

Glyph creation uses fontpr.set_glyph(create=True) and checks the created result; existing names are refused before the call. Components for a new glyph travel in its creation data. Adding components to existing layers requires a qualified plain component prototype. Creation can use multiple native steps; do not promise one Undo for the whole workflow. Unmeasured automatic-layer rebuilding stays guarded.

Earlier releases have bounded native receipts in CHANGELOG. Those receipts do not qualify later shared writers or the full migration. Zone serializer ABI/payload preservation remains open; the route-A zone and metrics writers have no native receipt yet. Current text, NUL/IME, printer/OS, cache/history, font preservation and UI lifecycle holds are listed in TODO. Native proof requires installed artifacts in owned FontLab fixtures, exact source hashes, complete state comparison, real controls, Undo/Redo and saved reopening for writers. Source and standalone Qt checks do not qualify native behavior.

Factory Purpose font_info_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None) Stage font information groups_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None) Edit groups kerning_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None) Inspect/edit kerning transform_editor(font, name=None, parent=None, on_change=None) Preview affine glyph transforms batch_panel(recipe, parent=None, on_finish=None, python=None) Run a UFO recipe in a child interpreter glyph_sequence(font, parent=None, on_select=None) Preview placed glyph sequences

docs.title: Demo scripts
docs.text:
Scripts/<Category>/<Tool> Demo.py holds small GUI demos of the App modules, one menu entry each (146 in 15 categories). install.vfpy copies them into FontLab's Scripts menu; the Demo.py suffix keeps them apart from Fly's Scriptmix scripts when both are installed. Demos import App through fly.ap and keep native imports lazy inside main(). They write nothing by themselves: no font, selection, history, preference, Output or clipboard, and no menu action is triggered. The exceptions start with your own click: the Copy buttons of Glyph Map and Common Glyphs write the clipboard; Proof Tabs, Kerning Proofs and Text Filter open a text tab only after you confirm or tick a box; Image Viewer's Print can write a PDF to a path you pick; and Text Holder, Text Filter and Image Viewer keep files in fixed fontlabapp-demos/<demo> folders under the system temp directory. Each script's Safety paragraph gives the details. tests/test_demo_scripts.py checks every file's layout, header and Fly imports by AST; tests/_demo_support.py runs a demo offline under stubbed natives. Four demos show core features in use rather than by name: Shim Generator (core.shimgen), Native Tabs (core.native_tabs), History Preflight (core.history) and Owned Lifetime (core.completion and the fontlabapp.ui factories); the last one adds a small panel to the main window (it may float) and removes it on close. Native FontLab acceptance of the demos is pending. tests/test_demo_scripts_coverage.py fails when a fontlabapp.<domain>.<feature> module has no demo naming it.

Named but not run, and why. The coverage test counts a module that a demo names, so some are named or summarised without running, for these reasons:

  • components.panel, contours.panel, anchors.panel and guides.rewrite hold the writer panels of the component, contour, anchor and guide scripts, and contours.copy and anchors.edit copy contours and run point transactions. Their buttons change glyphs, so Component Writers, Contour Panels, Anchor Plans and Guide Plans compute the plans on made-up data and only name the panels.
  • core.hotkey: its macOS HotkeyManager creates a session-wide Quartz event tap and needs the Accessibility permission, and on Windows it raises NotImplementedError. A demo would register global hotkeys, so Signals And Hotkeys only reports whether the backend can load.
  • core.legacy: examples launches relocated scripts with runpy, and vanilla is a tombstone that raises ImportError naming Glyport. Core Utilities shows their summaries.
  • fontlabapp.ui.actions, canvas, dialogs, panels, widgets and windows re-export objects of qt and core. Owned Lifetime runs create_widget, create_panel and create_dialog through that facade; the rest need live native objects or act on FontLab (actions triggers menu items, canvas registers painters on the glyph editor, windows wraps native glyph and preview windows), so Toolkit Reference lists their __all__ only.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Run from this repository. Set FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH to an existing writable directory on your external scratch volume. Use a fresh writable cache and an existing writable TMPDIR there. uv needs network access for packages not cached. Build from reviewed Git history so hatch-vcs supplies the genuine version required by the local Fontport/Glyport dependency floor. Do not reuse a cache containing App metadata from another build.

: "${FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH:?Set FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH to your external scratch directory}"
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH/app-doc-check-cache"
export TMPDIR="$FONTLAB_TEST_SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$UV_CACHE_DIR" "$TMPDIR"
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1
uv venv --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none "$TMPDIR/app-venv"
uv pip install --python "$TMPDIR/app-venv/bin/python" -e '.[test]'
uv pip install --python "$TMPDIR/app-venv/bin/python" -e ../fontlab-fontport -e ../fontlab-glyport
uv pip install --python "$TMPDIR/app-venv/bin/python" --no-deps -e ../fontlab-fly
"$TMPDIR/app-venv/bin/python" -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider

Install Fontport and Glyport with their dependencies (defcon, fissix, fontpens, glyphsLib); without them two tests fail. The tests of the FontParts editors (tests/test_ui_*.py, tests/test_cov_ui_*.py) call pytest.importorskip("fontlab_fontport"): they skip, not fail, when Fontport is absent, so a plain ./test.sh run does not exercise them. ./test.sh installs the sibling Fontport and Glyport checkouts editable and puts the sibling Fly source on PYTHONPATH when they exist, so it runs the whole suite; the test extra itself does not list Fontport.

The plain test-extra environment previously gave 6240 passes and three failures because Fly was missing. ./test.sh uses uv run --extra test with editable sibling Fontport/Glyport when available and sibling Fly on PYTHONPATH; the explicit environment above also verifies an installed Fly. Use the explicit command for the full suite. pytest reads tests/ and adds src to its import path.

At the dated source snapshot, there was no separate tests_docs/ suite. The current site now has the separate documentation checks described on the development page. With the same exports, run the README migration contract and public-surface/dependency checks:

uv run --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none --no-project --with-editable '.[test]' python -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_public_surface.py tests/test_package_boundaries.py tests/test_tombstones.py
uv run --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none --no-project --with-editable '.[test]' python -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_public_surface.py::test_readme_when_read_then_moved_table_names_every_tombstone
uv run --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none --no-project --with ruff==0.14.10 ruff check --no-cache --select F821 src tests Scripts

The lint command checks undefined names; there is no configured full lint gate. Offline tests cover Python logic and doubles. Standalone Qt uses a different binding. Neither establishes native FontLab acceptance.

docs.title: CurrentGlyph and editing boundaries
docs.text: A valid FontGate CurrentGlyph can be falsey when it has no contours. Glyph identity checks match the font ID and glyph name: CurrentGlyph().id can differ from the canvas slot ID for the same glyph. In an active Glyph window, a multi-glyph notifyChangesApplied Undo step attaches only to the canvas glyphs; other glyphs can keep the change and newly created glyphs can lack Undo. Shared edit_guards.require_history_scope guards refuse unsupported scopes. Close Glyph windows before a .vfc save. These native limitations remain distinct from source and standalone Qt test results; the historical consolidation-only CurrentGlyph exception does not waive current preservation or native qualification.
